evidence.quote: At this time, I see risks as tilted toward higher inflation.
until I see stronger evidence that inflation is moving sustainably back down to target, that is where my focus will be, in the absence of unexpected changes in the labor market.
Those readings indicate that progress on inflation essentially stalled in 2025.
the longer inflation remains above target, the greater the probability that higher inflation will become entrenched in expectations.
Overall, these readings indicate to me that the labor market is roughly in balance, but I am highly attentive to developments, knowing it can shift quickly.
But they do not, in my view, reveal a signal about increased slack that we can tackle with our typical demand-side monetary policy.

parsed.rationale: The speaker sees risks tilted toward higher inflation, emphasizes that inflation progress has stalled, and stresses credibility, which implies a hold with no near-term cuts. Labor-market risks and K-shaped strains are acknowledged, which tempers the hawkish lean.
